newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Allianz to fully take over Vereinte.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Allianz to fully take over Vereinte.

text.p: Insurance giant Allianz AG Holding on Tuesday got the green light for a full takeover of Vereinte Holding AG, ending two years of uncertainty about the health insurance unit's future.
Allianz acquired a majority stake in Vereinte in late 1994, but was not initially given clearance for a full takeover of the unit because of concerns by German monopoly authorities.

However, Germany's Berlin-based cartel office said Tuesday it had approved Allianz's plans to take over 100 percent of Vereinte, as well as its related plans to take over loan insurer Hermes Kreditversicherungs AG.

The news follows Allianz's surprise announcement earlier this year of plans to sell off its own health subsidiary Deutsche Krankenversicherungs AG (DKV), easing cartel office worries about the strength of its position on the German health insurance market.
"This means we can proceed in integrating these two companies in a way which will bring benefits for our customers," an Allianz spokesman said.

Allianz arranged to sell DKV and acquire Hermes and additional holdings in Vereinte in a complex share swap arranged with Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG, the reinsurance group with which Allianz has close links.
Allianz received Munich Re's majority stake in Hermes as well as stakes in the Vereinte group's private health insurance unit and in Allianz's Austrian activities in the deal.
Analysts said the arrangement was a pragmatic solution to the vexed question of Vereinte's ownership and could promise better earnings for Allianz.
Allianz had been widely expected to sell Vereinte, which it had acquired from Swiss Re in October 1994 as part of a package of three primary insurers in Italy, Switzerland and Germany.

German cartel authorities had argued that ownership of both DKV and Vereinte, which is Germany's second largest health insurer, would have given Allianz a stranglehold on the German health insurance market.
On Tuesday, a spokeswoman for the cartel office confirmed that approval for the moves had been given, but declined to give any further details.
The EU Commission, which has already approved the Hermes deal, has also approved the Vereinte takeover, according to sources there.
